cards.front: If you hold no license from California or any other state, what must you have before the behind-the-wheel drive test?
cards.back: Without a license from California or another state, you must hold an instruction permit before you may take the behind-the-wheel drive test.

cards.front: What proof must every permit or license application include?
cards.back: A permit or license application must include proof of identity showing who you are.

cards.front: How many proofs of California residency must you show?
cards.back: You must also show two proofs that you live in California, though exceptions may apply.

cards.front: What must you add when the name on your identity document differs from your application?
cards.back: When the name on your identity document differs from your application, you must add a legal full name document proving your current name.

cards.front: Which number is required with a permit or license application?
cards.back: A social security number is required as well, with exceptions possible.

cards.front: Where are the current REAL ID document rules and eligibility posted?
cards.back: Current REAL ID document rules and eligibility are posted at dmv.ca.gov slash realid.

cards.front: Who handles voter registration in California?
cards.back: Voter registration runs through the California Secretary of State at sos.ca.gov.

cards.front: What separate job does each of the four application proofs do?
cards.back: Four proofs do four jobs: identity says who you are, two residency proofs say you live in California, the name document bridges mismatched names, and the social security number identifies the record.

decks.module: Steps to a Class C permit

cards.front: What is the first step toward a Class C permit?
cards.back: A Class C permit starts with a completed Driver's License and ID Card Application.

cards.front: What comes next after the completed application for a Class C permit?
cards.back: Next you hand over your documents and pay a non-refundable application fee.

cards.front: Which tests must you pass for a Class C permit?
cards.back: Then you must pass your knowledge test or tests plus a vision test.

cards.front: Where is the full list of permit steps and requirements kept?
cards.back: The full permit steps and requirements list lives at dmv.ca.gov slash instructionpermit.

cards.front: What comes before any drive test for the unlicensed, and what steps make up the permit?
cards.back: The unlicensed start with a permit before any drive test, and that permit itself takes five ordered steps: application, documents, fee, knowledge tests, vision test.

cards.front: Which parts of the permit process are tests, and which are paperwork?
cards.back: The permit demands two test passes, knowledge and vision, while documents and fees are paperwork rather than tests.

cards.front: How old must an applicant under eighteen be to get a permit?
cards.back: Applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen and a half years old for a permit.

cards.front: What program must a minor finish to get a permit?
cards.back: Those minors must also finish a driver education program.

cards.front: Who must sign a minor's application, and what do they accept?
cards.back: A parent or guardian must sign the minor's application, accepting financial responsibility, and both parents must sign under joint custody.

cards.front: When may a minor start using the instruction permit?
cards.back: The minor may not use the permit until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it.

cards.front: Where do driver education and training come from, and what should you ask the instructor to show?
cards.back: Driver education and training come from DMV-licensed driving schools and some high schools, whose instructors must carry an instructor ID card you should ask to see.

cards.front: Where can you find guidance on choosing a driving school?
cards.back: Guidance on choosing a driving school sits at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-ed.

decks.module: Practice and the step to a license

cards.front: Who must sit beside you during permit practice?
cards.back: Permit practice needs a California-licensed driver at least eighteen years old, or twenty-five for minors, sitting close enough to seize control.

cards.front: How do the supervisor age rules differ for adults and minors?
cards.back: Practice supervisors split by age: eighteen-plus suffices for adults, but minors need a twenty-five-plus licensed driver.

cards.front: What must you still pass after the permit to get the license itself?
cards.back: After the permit, the license itself still requires passing a behind-the-wheel drive test.

cards.front: How old must a minor be to move from permit to license?
cards.back: Minors must be at least sixteen years old to move from permit to license.

cards.front: How long must a minor hold an instruction permit before the license, and what is the alternative?
cards.back: They must also have held an instruction permit for at least six months, from California or another state, or else turn eighteen before booking the drive test.

cards.front: Which two things must a minor prove they finished before getting a license?
cards.back: They must prove they finished both driver education and driver training.

cards.front: How does driver education differ from driver training?
cards.back: Driver education is the program minors must complete, while driver training is the in-car instruction whose instructor validates the permit.

cards.front: How many practice hours must a minor log, and how many at night?
cards.back: They must log at least fifty practice hours with a California-licensed driver aged twenty-five or more, including ten hours at night.

cards.front: What are the rungs of the teen ladder from permit to license?
cards.back: The teen ladder runs fifteen-and-a-half for the permit, sixteen for the license, a six-month permit hold, and fifty practice hours with ten at night.

cards.front: Where are teen steps, the Parent Teen Driving Contract and the score sheet collected?
cards.back: Teen steps, requirements, the Parent Teen Driving Contract, and the Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Score Sheet are collected at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver.

cards.front: Which word appears on a license issued before age eighteen?
cards.back: Licenses issued before age eighteen carry the word provisional.

cards.front: During which hours may a provisional driver not drive in the first year?
cards.back: A provisional driver may not drive between eleven p.m. and five a.m. during the first twelve months of licensure.

cards.front: Whom may a provisional driver not carry without a qualified adult along?
cards.back: Nor may they carry passengers under twenty unless a parent, guardian, or California-licensed driver at least twenty-five years old rides along.

cards.front: What kinds of driving are off-limits to a provisional driver?
cards.back: Provisional drivers may not drive for pay nor operate vehicles needing a commercial Class A, B, or C license.

cards.front: What three bans bind every provisional driver?
cards.back: Three bans bind every provisional driver: no late-night driving, no young passengers without a qualified rider, and no paid or commercial driving.

cards.front: What must a provisional driver carry to use the medical-need exception?
cards.back: A medical-need exception requires a physician-signed note in the car stating the condition and the expected recovery date.

cards.front: Who must sign the note for the school driving exception?
cards.back: School driving needs a note signed by the principal, dean, or designee.

cards.front: What note does the work driving exception need?
cards.back: Work driving needs an employer-signed note confirming the employment.

cards.front: What must the note for driving an immediate family member include, and who signs it?
cards.back: Driving an immediate family member needs a parent or guardian-signed note naming the reason, the member, and the end date.

cards.front: Who signs the note for each of the four provisional exceptions?
cards.back: Four exceptions need four different signers: physician for medical need, principal or dean for school, employer for work, and parent or guardian for family.

cards.front: How can a parent or guardian cancel a teen's license?
cards.back: A parent or guardian can cancel a teen's license by filing a Request for Cancellation or Surrender of a Driver License or ID Card form.

cards.front: What marks the teen license, and who can cancel it?
cards.back: The provisional word marks the teen license, and the same parents behind it can cancel it outright with the surrender form.

recap_hooks.text: Without any license you need a permit before the drive test, and the application carries proof of identity, two residency proofs, a social security number and, if names differ, a legal name document.

recaps.module: Steps to a Class C permit

recap_hooks.text: A Class C permit runs in order: the application, then documents and the non-refundable fee, then the knowledge and vision tests.
Only the knowledge and vision tests are tests; the rest is paperwork.
A minor needs to be at least fifteen and a half, finish driver education and have a parent or guardian sign before the permit.
The permit is not usable until training begins with an instructor who validates it.

recaps.module: Practice and the step to a license

recap_hooks.text: Practice needs a licensed driver at least eighteen, or at least twenty-five for minors, close enough to take control.
A minor's license needs age sixteen, six months with a permit or turning eighteen, proof of education and training, and fifty practice hours with ten at night.
A license issued before eighteen is provisional, with no late-night driving in the first year, no passengers under twenty without a qualified adult, and no paid or commercial driving.
Each exception needs its own signed note: physician for medical need, school official for school, employer for work, and parent or guardian for family.
A parent or guardian can cancel a teen's license by filing the cancellation form.
